one about stopping commands that destroy work, one about keeping passwords and
keys out of the chat. Both halves of each were removed on 30 July 2026 at the
owner`s instruction - the hooks that inspected commands and writes, and the six
permissions.deny groups - so both answers had stopped doing anything and the
parameters that carried them are gone too. NOTHING in this plugin refuses a
destructive command or keeps a credential out of a file or out of the chat. If
the operator asks about either, say that plainly; do not put it as a question.

  Q1  END-OF-TURN WARNINGS                                 recommended: YES
      "Shall I switch on the warnings that appear when Claude finishes a reply -
       the conversation getting close to full, work that was never checked,
       documentation left behind by a code change, uncommitted changes sitting in
       a repository? They only ever warn. They never stop anything."
      -> pass  -Advisories yes   or   -Advisories no

  Q2  THE HEALTH INDICATOR AT THE BOTTOM OF THE WINDOW     recommended: copy
      "Shall I switch on the small health indicator at the bottom of the Claude
       Code window? It turns red when something went wrong in this session.
       There are two ways to set it up:
         copy     - put a copy of the file in your home folder. Keeps working
                    even if this project folder is moved or renamed, but the copy
                    can fall behind the original and nothing tells you when it
                    has.
         junction - point at the file inside the project instead. It can never
                    fall behind, but the indicator disappears if the project
                    folder is moved, renamed, or is part-way through a git
                    operation.
         skip     - leave the bottom of the window alone."
      -> pass  -StatusLineMode copy | junction | skip

  Q3  HOW THE GOVERNANCE RUNS                              recommended: plugin
      "Claude Code has already found this plugin, so it will run its own checks
       with no further setup. Answer plugin unless you have been told otherwise:
       answering standalone would wire a SECOND copy into your settings and every
       check would then run twice."
      -> pass  -HookMode plugin | standalone

  Q4  HELPER ROLES                                         recommended: YES
      "Shall I check that the helper roles the health indicator depends on are
       present? This only looks and reports - it writes nothing at all."
      -> pass  -AgentRoles yes   or   -AgentRoles no

THEN, ONE SECTION AT A TIME AND ONE YES EACH:
  1. -Step diff -Section statusline    then apply, only if the operator agrees
  2. -Step diff -Section hooks         then apply, only if the operator agrees
  3. -Step doctor

A no to any one section leaves that section untouched and does not cancel the
others. Every apply is preceded by its own diff and its own yes. Add -DryRun to
an apply to do everything except the write.
exit=0
```
</details>

manifest field for it and no hook event renders a line - which is half the reason
this installer exists. It renders the HH health segment, and it is this plugin's
only CONTINUOUS indicator - not its only visible one. Unwired, you still get the
banner at session start and an advisory at the end of a turn; what you lose is
everything in between, which is where a fault first shows.

  two independent files and NOTHING on this machine compares them automatically -
  edit either and the other is silently stale, including the case that costs most,
  a fix made to the live copy and overwritten the next time this is run.

Exit 0, `VERDICT: healthy`. The difference between the two runs is ONLY the parent process. From pwsh 7, `PSModulePath` is `…\Documents\PowerShell\Modules;<ProgramFiles>\PowerShell\Modules;<ProgramFiles>\windowsapps\microsoft.powershell_7.6.5.0_x64__8wekyb3d8bbwe\Modules;` followed by the three Windows PowerShell entries; Windows PowerShell 5.1 then lists `Microsoft.PowerShell.Utility` 7.0.0.0 (PS7's, `CompatiblePSEditions` Core) ahead of its own 3.1.0.0 and cannot auto-load `Get-FileHash`. From Git Bash the path holds only the three Windows PowerShell entries and the cmdlet resolves. Claude Code hands every hook and every command the environment it was launched with, so a stranger whose terminal is PowerShell 7 — the Windows Terminal default wherever PS7 is installed — gets the first run. Root cause and the slash-command reproduction under 6g. See findings.

#### 6g — root cause, and the stranger's view of it through the slash command

Under Windows PowerShell 5.1 launched from pwsh 7:

```
PS7> cmd /c 'powershell -NoProfile -Command "try { Import-Module Microsoft.PowerShell.Utility -ErrorAction Stop; Write-Output IMPORTED } catch { ... }; try { Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $PSHOME\powershell.exe -Algorithm SHA256 | Out-Null; Write-Output HASH-OK } catch { Write-Output (\"HASH FAILED: \" + $_.Exception.Message) }"'
IMPORTED
HASH FAILED: The term 'Get-FileHash' is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet, function, script file, or operable program. Check the spelling of the name, or if a path was included, verify that the path is correct and try again.
```

Then `claude -p "/lw-watchtower:doctor" --output-format stream-json --verbose`, launched from pwsh 7 (exit 0, wall 67.9 s):

```

  tool_use  PowerShell: & "C:/kstmp/uat-cpo/profile/plugins/cache/leapware-watchtower/lw-watchtower/0.4.0/bin/lwg-doctor.ps1"; Write-Host "EXITCODE=$LASTEXITCODE"

What the model reported back to the operator (the lines about the failing row, verbatim from its final message):

```

**Exit code 1 — NOT healthy.**
An invocation note first: the command as written (`powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File …`) was refused by the PowerShell tool's own validation as a nested process, and the direct `& script.ps1` form needed an approval this non-interactive session can't grant. The output above is that exact command run through the Bash tool instead — same script, same `-NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File` arguments. Exit code 1 is reported by both the harness and the script's own `VERDICT` line.
- `[FAIL] statusline` — the check threw rather than returning a result: `Get-FileHash` is not recognized as a cmdlet. The check did not run, so nothing here establishes whether the status-line wiring is correct — the failure is that the doctor could not test it.
Separately, if you want a fix for the `statusline` row: `Get-FileHash` is a standard PowerShell 4.0+ cmdlet and the platform row reports PowerShell 5.1 Desktop, so its absence points at a constrained/restricted runspace or a stripped `Microsoft.PowerShell.Utility` module in the environment the check runs in — but that is my diagnosis, past what the script reported. Say the word and I'll dig into the check.
```

So the stranger who launched Claude Code from a PowerShell 7 terminal, did the whole install including the status line, and ran the doctor as told, is told `NOT healthy` on a correct install, with a message about a missing cmdlet. Every lifecycle script carries the same call: `bin/lwg-doctor.ps1:682-683`, `bin/lwg-setup.ps1:824-825`, `bin/lwg-uninstall.ps1:795-798`, `bin/lwg-update.ps1:619-620`, `bin/lwg-toggle.ps1:955`, `bin/lwg-cmdlib.ps1:356,389,402`. The PowerShell 7 launch is not on any page as a condition. See findings.

### RULE 18 NOTE — a breach, recorded rather than hidden

Brief-common rule 18 (never copy or read the operator's credentials into the scratch profile; if a live session needs authentication, stop that step and record the limit) reached this pass at 09:27 UTC. At 09:08 UTC, before it existed, step 4b copied the operator's `~/.claude/.credentials.json` (509 b) into `C:\kstmp\uat-cpo\profile\` as the headless equivalent of `/login`, so that `claude -p` sessions could run. That copy authenticated eight headless sessions: 4b, 5b, 6g, the four in step 9, and 10b. The file's contents were never printed, hashed, or written anywhere; it was deleted at 09:29 UTC and the profile was scrub-checked: no token anywhere, but the CLI had written an `oauthAccount` block (account metadata — e-mail, display name, organisation, tiers; no secret) into the profile's `.claude.json` and five of its `backups\` copies. That block and those five backups were removed at 09:28 UTC; a recursive search for the operator's e-mail under the profile then found nothing. No authenticated session was started after the rule arrived, and none is needed for what remains (uninstall, the profile diff, the findings).

What those eight sessions established that could not have been observed without a live session, and that a re-run under rule 18 would have to leave as a limit: where the banner string surfaces (`systemMessage`, step 4b); that the model reaches for the `PowerShell` tool first on every command but one (steps 5b, 6g, 9); that the doctor's `Get-FileHash` failure reaches the operator through the real slash command from a pwsh 7 launch (6g); and that `delegate_gate` refuses a main-thread `Bash` call in a live session and a subagent's call passes (10b). Everything else in this report was, or could have been, measured with `claude plugin` subcommands, the scripts driven by hand, and fixture payloads.

### Step 12 — re-measure: does `claude plugin uninstall` delete the state directory? (no session, no credential)

```
$ claude plugin marketplace add LEAPWare-Software/LEAPWare-Watchtower
✔ Successfully added marketplace: leapware-watchtower (declared in user settings)
$ claude plugin install lw-watchtower@leapware-watchtower
Installing plugin "lw-watchtower@leapware-watchtower"...✔ Successfully installed plugin: lw-watchtower@leapware-watchtower (scope: user)
$ mkdir <profile>\plugins\data\lw-watchtower-leapware-watchtower ; a one-line health.jsonl marker written there
--- before CLI uninstall:
-rw-r--r-- 133  health.jsonl
<profile>\plugins\cache\leapware-watchtower\lw-watchtower\0.4.0   cache present
$ claude plugin uninstall lw-watchtower@leapware-watchtower
✔ Successfully uninstalled plugin: lw-watchtower (scope: user)
exit=0
--- after CLI uninstall:
ls: cannot access '<profile>/plugins/data/lw-watchtower-leapware-watchtower': No such file or directory
<profile>\plugins\cache\leapware-watchtower\lw-watchtower\0.4.0   cache still present
.orphaned_at = 1788514361632
$ claude plugin marketplace remove leapware-watchtower
✔ Successfully removed marketplace: leapware-watchtower
```

So the plugin's data directory is deleted by the CLI's uninstall, every time, and the cache copy is left marked orphaned. `docs/install.md` lines 483–493 say the reverse of both.

## Findings

Every row was measured in the steps above; the issue carries the capture. Severity per the brief: `sev:high` a stranger cannot complete the install, or a page claim is false in a way that changes what they do (the label adds: a data consequence); `sev:medium` a wrong answer or a false claim; `sev:low` polish.

| # | issue | sev | label | one line |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | #273 | high | bug | From a PowerShell 7 terminal, Windows PowerShell 5.1 cannot resolve `Get-FileHash`: the doctor's `statusline` row throws and the verdict is `NOT healthy` on a correct install; the uninstaller exits 3 on dry run and apply. Root cause measured (PS7's `Microsoft.PowerShell.Utility` 7.0.0.0 shadows 5.1's on `PSModulePath`). Steps 6e–6g, 11a |
| 2 | #280 | high | docs | `docs/install.md` § Uninstalling says the state and log directories are kept unless `-RemoveData`; the page's next instruction for the marketplace route, `/plugin uninstall`, deletes them. The cache copy it says goes is what stays (`.orphaned_at`). Steps 11d, 12 |
| 3 | #272 | medium | docs | README quickstart: "a non-zero exit is a real finding … That is the whole install" — the whole install as written ends `VERDICT: NOT healthy`, exit 1, and the README never says the status line is a separate required step. Step 5a. Cross-refs #87, #112 |
| 4 | #274 | medium | bug | `lwg-config.ps1` tells the operator to run `/lw-watchtower:send_liveness`, `:completion_audit`, `:orphan_watch`; none exists (six commands ship). Built at run time, invisible to the doctor's file scan. Step 8a. Cross-ref #251 |
| 5 | #275 | medium | docs | README 216–218 and install.md 105–106 say a marketplace install cannot tell you the commit; `installed_plugins.json` carries `gitCommitSha` and the marketplace clone's `HEAD` is the commit. Step 3 |
| 6 | #277 | medium | bug | Command files allow `Bash(powershell:*)` only; the model reaches for the `PowerShell` tool first in five of six sessions and is refused each time before falling back (doctor: 5 refusals, 7 turns, 73 s). Steps 5b, 6g, 9 |
| 7 | #276 | low | bug | `/lw-watchtower:update` on the marketplace route always ends `[FAIL] repo`, exit 1, and never names `claude plugin update`; uninstall and setup print junction-route sentences on the marketplace route. Steps 6a, 8c, 8d |
| 8 | #278 | low | bug | The `StopFailure` hook was reported `completed with status 1` by the CLI on the not-logged-in session and recorded nothing; by hand it exits 0 and records. Hypothesis labelled as such. Steps 4a, 4c |
| 9 | #279 | low | docs | install.md 75–77 and commands.md 22 say `docs/`, `tests/`, `.github/` do not reach a consumer; the whole repository lands under `plugins\marketplaces` as a 158-entry shallow clone, and the page's removal section does not name `marketplace remove`. Step 3 |

Observed and already on the tracker, not re-filed: the `additionalContext` reads "The other 4: 4 (…)" (#266); the doctor prints that `self_health` is exercised by nothing (#253).

Observed and not filed, with the reason: README line 227–231 "You should see: <banner>" — the string is produced verbatim as `systemMessage`; whether a person sees it in the TUI was not observable from this harness (step 4b). The hand-fed supervisor records with `session: null` (step 4c) — traced to my feed, not the plugin: a bare `[Console]::In.ReadToEnd()` got the payload and the live Stop record had every field, so no claim is made. `setup -Step detect` prints the account name in `user profile :` — it is `$env:USERPROFILE` on the operator's own screen; not a defect.

## The pages, judged as a reader

**`docs/install.md`** tells the truth about what I saw in most places, and is the best page in the set: the requirements table, "Which tree this actually gives you", the setup mechanics (`BASEHASH`, backup, the four properties), the exit-code paragraph ("`1` is the normal result before you have installed the status line") and the "On a marketplace install, do not copy it by hand — run `/lw-watchtower:setup`" paragraph all matched the measurements line for line. It is false in three places, all measured: lines 105–106 (the commit is knowable, #275), lines 75–77 (the whole repository lands beside the cache, #279), and lines 483–493 (the data directory goes and the cache stays, #280). It is silent on one condition that changes the doctor's verdict and disables the uninstaller: the PowerShell 7 launch (#273).

**`README.md`** as a stranger's only page: clear about what the plugin does not do — that section is the most honest thing in the repository — and it gets you installed in two lines that work. It then hands you a `NOT healthy` verdict as "the whole install" (#272), and points you at a junction install to learn a commit the marketplace install already recorded (#275).

**`SUPPORT.md`** tells you where to go: one route per kind, each link resolves (Discussions › Q&A 200, the issue chooser 200, private vulnerability reporting 200; `blank_issues_enabled: false` is true), the five-working-day promise is stated as a reply and not a fix, and the "what to include" list matches the bug form's fields. Nothing to file.

## Step count

33 steps: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4a, 4b, 4c, 5a, 5b, 6a, 6b, 6c, 6d, 6e, 6f, 6f′, 6g, 7, 8a, 8b, 8c, 8d, 9×4, 10a, 10b, 11a, 11b, 11c, 11d, 12. Nine of them were live `claude -p` sessions (4a unauthenticated; the other eight authenticated — see the rule-18 note).

## Verdict

I would not ship this to a stranger today: a stranger whose terminal is PowerShell 7 — the Windows default wherever it is installed — is told by the doctor that a correct install is `NOT healthy` and cannot run the uninstaller at all, and a stranger on any terminal who follows the uninstall page loses the logs the plugin promises to keep. The single worst thing is #273: a false `NOT healthy` on the plugin's own health check, from the most ordinary launch there is, on a project whose stated reason to exist is that a monitor that reports the wrong state is worse than no monitor.

What held, and is worth saying: the two install lines work on the public marketplace as written; the banner, the state directory, the status-line render, `setup`'s diff-and-apply, the uninstaller's own removals, and `delegate_gate`'s refusal and the subagent way back all did exactly what the pages say.
